sections.content:
65,425 people

were counted on the census as "data analysts" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Data analysts gather and organise a variety of data and analyse it to understand what it means for their organisation or society.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "data analysts", 22.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "data analysts" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "data analysts" included:

  • human resources and industrial relations officers
  • business and related research professionals
  • graphic and multimedia designers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "data analysts" there were more men than women (58.6% compared with 41.4%).

This means "data analysts" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 58.6% and women made up 41.4% of "data analysts"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "data analysts" included:

  • managers and proprietors in other services (other)
  • environment professionals
  • specialist medical practitioners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "data analysts" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "data analysts" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "data analysts", 8.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (90.1% compared with 9.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.6%) than self-employed (3.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
